differs.fact: The importation bond (19 CFR 113.62) binds the importer to file every ISF in the manner and time the rule sets; a default costs liquidated damages of $5,000 for each violation, paid by the importer and its surety. So each ocean shipment's ISF goes in at least 24 hours before it is loaded abroad, every time.
differs.agency: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (19 CFR part 113)
differs.quote: the principal and surety (jointly and severally) agree to pay liquidated damages of $5,000 for each violation.

differs.fact: Under the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act, CBP presumes that goods made by an entity on the UFLPA Entity List are made with forced labor and keeps them out. Before the first order, Odelia checks your factories and their wood, fabric and foam suppliers against the list.
differs.agency: U.S. Department of Homeland Security (Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force)
differs.quote: apply a rebuttable presumption that goods mined, produced, or manufactured by entities on the UFLPA Entity List are made with forced labor,

differs.fact: Certain upholstered wooden products entering since October 14, 2025 pay a 25 percent Section 232 tariff on top of other duties. The rise to 30 percent for upholstered furniture was moved to January 1, 2027, except for countries with an agreement. Price your landed cost with it.
differs.agency: The President (Proclamation 11000), collected by U.S. Customs and Border Protection
differs.quote: a 25 percent ad valorem tariff on imports of certain upholstered wooden products, kitchen cabinets, and vanities.

differs.fact: Ohio requires anyone making or wholesaling upholstered furniture sold in Ohio to register with its Division of Industrial Compliance, $50 a year, wherever the business is based. If you sell into Ohio, register before your first sale there.
differs.agency: Ohio Department of Commerce, Division of Industrial Compliance
differs.quote: Any person who engages in manufacturing or wholesaling bedding or upholstered furniture that is to be sold or offered for sale in this state;

differs.quote: must include the fabricator’s name, the date the finished good was produced (in month/year format), and a TSCA Title VI compliance statement.

differs.fact: Furniture can expose people to chemicals on California's Proposition 65 list: formaldehyde from composite wood and coatings, flame retardants in foam and fabric, phthalates in vinyl, PFOA and PFOS in stain-resistant upholstery. The business determines whether a warning is required before selling in California.
differs.agency: California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment
differs.quote: Proposition 65 requires businesses to determine if they must provide a warning about significant exposure to listed chemicals.

differs.fact: Upholstered furniture sold in California carries a law label naming the manufacturer, its location (by registry number) and the filling materials, attached before it is offered for sale.
differs.agency: California Bureau of Household Goods and Services
differs.quote: Every article of upholstered furniture and bedding products must have a law label to identify the manufacturer,

differs.fact: Upholstered furniture also carries a flammability label naming the standard it meets. Furniture meeting Technical Bulletin 117-2013 states on that label whether its materials contain added flame retardant chemicals.
differs.agency: California Bureau of Household Goods and Services
differs.quote: Products meeting Technical Bulletin 117-2013 must also have the flammability chemical statement on the label.

differs.fact: Furniture can expose people to chemicals on California's Proposition 65 list: formaldehyde from composite wood and coatings, flame retardants in foam and fabric, phthalates in vinyl, PFOA and PFOS in stain-resistant upholstery. The business determines whether a warning is required before selling in California.
differs.agency: California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment
differs.quote: Proposition 65 requires businesses to determine if they must provide a warning about significant exposure to listed chemicals.

differs.fact: Upholstered furniture sold in California carries a law label naming the manufacturer, its location (by registry number) and the filling materials, attached before it is offered for sale.

differs.fact: Upholstered furniture also carries a flammability label naming the standard it meets. Furniture meeting Technical Bulletin 117-2013 states on that label whether its materials contain added flame retardant chemicals.
differs.agency: California Bureau of Household Goods and Services
differs.quote: Products meeting Technical Bulletin 117-2013 must also have the flammability chemical statement on the label.

differs.fact: The importation bond (19 CFR 113.62) binds the importer to file every ISF in the manner and time the rule sets; a default costs liquidated damages of $5,000 for each violation, paid by the importer and its surety. So each ocean shipment's ISF goes in at least 24 hours before it is loaded abroad, every time.
differs.agency: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (19 CFR part 113)
differs.quote: the principal and surety (jointly and severally) agree to pay liquidated damages of $5,000 for each violation.

differs.fact: Under the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act, CBP presumes that goods made by an entity on the UFLPA Entity List are made with forced labor and keeps them out. Before the first order, Odelia checks your factories and their wood, fabric and foam suppliers against the list.
differs.agency: U.S. Department of Homeland Security (Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force)
differs.quote: apply a rebuttable presumption that goods mined, produced, or manufactured by entities on the UFLPA Entity List are made with forced labor,

differs.fact: Certain upholstered wooden products entering since October 14, 2025 pay a 25 percent Section 232 tariff on top of other duties. The rise to 30 percent for upholstered furniture was moved to January 1, 2027, except for countries with an agreement. Price your landed cost with it.
differs.agency: The President (Proclamation 11000), collected by U.S. Customs and Border Protection
differs.quote: a 25 percent ad valorem tariff on imports of certain upholstered wooden products, kitchen cabinets, and vanities.

differs.fact: The importation bond (19 CFR 113.62) binds the importer to file every ISF in the manner and time the rule sets; a default costs liquidated damages of $5,000 for each violation, paid by the importer and its surety. So each ocean shipment's ISF goes in at least 24 hours before it is loaded abroad, every time.

differs.quote: the principal and surety (jointly and severally) agree to pay liquidated damages of $5,000 for each violation.

differs.fact: Under the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act, CBP presumes that goods made by an entity on the UFLPA Entity List are made with forced labor and keeps them out. Before the first order, Odelia checks your factories and their wood, fabric and foam suppliers against the list.
differs.agency: U.S. Department of Homeland Security (Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force)
differs.quote: apply a rebuttable presumption that goods mined, produced, or manufactured by entities on the UFLPA Entity List are made with forced labor,

differs.fact: Certain upholstered wooden products entering since October 14, 2025 pay a 25 percent Section 232 tariff on top of other duties. The rise to 30 percent for upholstered furniture was moved to January 1, 2027, except for countries with an agreement. Price your landed cost with it.
differs.agency: The President (Proclamation 11000), collected by U.S. Customs and Border Protection
differs.quote: a 25 percent ad valorem tariff on imports of certain upholstered wooden products, kitchen cabinets, and vanities.

differs.fact: The importation bond (19 CFR 113.62) binds the importer to file every ISF in the manner and time the rule sets; a default costs liquidated damages of $5,000 for each violation, paid by the importer and its surety. So each ocean shipment's ISF goes in at least 24 hours before it is loaded abroad, every time.
differs.agency: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (19 CFR part 113)
differs.quote: the principal and surety (jointly and severally) agree to pay liquidated damages of $5,000 for each violation.

differs.fact: Under the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act, CBP presumes that goods made by an entity on the UFLPA Entity List are made with forced labor and keeps them out. Before the first order, Odelia checks your factories and their wood, fabric and foam suppliers against the list.
differs.agency: U.S. Department of Homeland Security (Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force)
differs.quote: apply a rebuttable presumption that goods mined, produced, or manufactured by entities on the UFLPA Entity List are made with forced labor,

differs.fact: Certain upholstered wooden products entering since October 14, 2025 pay a 25 percent Section 232 tariff on top of other duties. The rise to 30 percent for upholstered furniture was moved to January 1, 2027, except for countries with an agreement. Price your landed cost with it.
differs.agency: The President (Proclamation 11000), collected by U.S. Customs and Border Protection
differs.quote: a 25 percent ad valorem tariff on imports of certain upholstered wooden products, kitchen cabinets, and vanities.

differs.fact: Ohio requires anyone making or wholesaling upholstered furniture sold in Ohio to register with its Division of Industrial Compliance, $50 a year, wherever the business is based. If you sell into Ohio, register before your first sale there.
differs.agency: Ohio Department of Commerce, Division of Industrial Compliance
differs.quote: Any person who engages in manufacturing or wholesaling bedding or upholstered furniture that is to be sold or offered for sale in this state;

differs.quote: a 25 percent ad valorem tariff on imports of certain upholstered wooden products, kitchen cabinets, and vanities.

differs.quote: a 25 percent ad valorem tariff on imports of certain upholstered wooden products, kitchen cabinets, and vanities.

differs.agency: The President (Proclamation 11000), collected by U.S. Customs and Border Protection
differs.quote: a 25 percent ad valorem tariff on imports of certain upholstered wooden products, kitchen cabinets, and vanities.

differs.fact: Furniture containing hardwood plywood, MDF or particleboard is labeled with the fabricator's name, the month and year it was produced, and a TSCA Title VI compliance statement. EPA's page names retailers among those the rule applies to.

differs.quote: must include the fabricator’s name, the date the finished good was produced (in month/year format), and a TSCA Title VI compliance statement.

differs.fact: Furniture can expose people to chemicals on California's Proposition 65 list: formaldehyde from composite wood and coatings, flame retardants in foam and fabric, phthalates in vinyl, PFOA and PFOS in stain-resistant upholstery. differs.agency: California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment
differs.quote: Proposition 65 requires businesses to determine if they must provide a warning about significant exposure to listed chemicals.

differs.fact: Upholstered furniture sold in California carries a law label naming the manufacturer, its location (by registry number) and the filling materials, attached before it is offered for sale.

differs.fact: Upholstered furniture also carries a flammability label naming the standard it meets. Furniture meeting Technical Bulletin 117-2013 states on that label whether its materials contain added flame retardant chemicals.
differs.agency: California Bureau of Household Goods and Services
differs.quote: Products meeting Technical Bulletin 117-2013 must also have the flammability chemical statement on the label.

differs.quote: the principal and surety (jointly and severally) agree to pay liquidated damages of $5,000 for each violation.

differs.fact: Furniture can expose people to chemicals on California's Proposition 65 list: formaldehyde from composite wood and coatings, flame retardants in foam and fabric, phthalates in vinyl, PFOA and PFOS in stain-resistant upholstery. differs.agency: California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment
differs.quote: Proposition 65 requires businesses to determine if they must provide a warning about significant exposure to listed chemicals.

differs.fact: Upholstered furniture sold in California carries a law label naming the manufacturer, its location (by registry number) and the filling materials, attached before it is offered for sale.

differs.fact: Upholstered furniture also carries a flammability label naming the standard it meets. Furniture meeting Technical Bulletin 117-2013 states on that label whether its materials contain added flame retardant chemicals.
differs.agency: California Bureau of Household Goods and Services
differs.quote: Products meeting Technical Bulletin 117-2013 must also have the flammability chemical statement on the label.

differs.fact: The importation bond (19 CFR 113.62) binds the importer to file every ISF in the manner and time the rule sets; a default costs liquidated damages of $5,000 for each violation, paid by the importer and its surety. So each ocean shipment's ISF goes in at least 24 hours before it is loaded abroad, every time.
differs.agency: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (19 CFR part 113)
differs.quote: the principal and surety (jointly and severally) agree to pay liquidated damages of $5,000 for each violation.

differs.fact: Under the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act, CBP presumes that goods made by an entity on the UFLPA Entity List are made with forced labor and keeps them out. Before the first order, Odelia checks your factories and their wood, fabric and foam suppliers against the list.
differs.agency: U.S. Department of Homeland Security (Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force)
differs.quote: apply a rebuttable presumption that goods mined, produced, or manufactured by entities on the UFLPA Entity List are made with forced labor,

differs.fact: Ohio requires anyone making or wholesaling upholstered furniture sold in Ohio to register with its Division of Industrial Compliance, $50 a year, wherever the business is based. If you sell into Ohio, register before your first sale there.
differs.agency: Ohio Department of Commerce, Division of Industrial Compliance
differs.quote: Any person who engages in manufacturing or wholesaling bedding or upholstered furniture that is to be sold or offered for sale in this state;
